question: Application of the Digital Services Act (DSA – Regulation (EU) 2022/2065) to content delivery network (CDN) services

As recognised by Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 itself, new technologies and services have emerged in recent decades ‘that improve the availability, efficiency, speed, reliability, capacity and security of systems for the transmission, ‘findability’ and storage of data online, leading to an increasingly complex online ecosystem’.

Doubts sometimes arise as to the legal nature of such services for the purposes of their qualification as ‘intermediaries’ in the area of digital services regulation and, therefore, as to their obligations to collaborate with the relevant authorities on removing or blocking illegal content, their place under the exemptions from liability and subjection to the DSA itself.

In light of the various judicial and administrative rulings in the Member States in application of the DSA and, where applicable, with the information included in the data-sharing platform between Digital Services Coordinators and the Commission (AGORA): 1.
Does the Commission consider CDN services to qualify as intermediary services under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065?
Which category would they fall under in Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, if any?
